chunks: My brother ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs ibn Aḥmad, from ‘Imrān ibn Mūsā, from Ḥasan ibn Mūsā Al-Khashab, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥassān, from his uncle ‘Abdil Raḥmān ibn Kuthayr, who said: I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say:

I heard him (the Imam) say to Abā Ḥamzah Al-Thumāli, 'O Abā Ḥamzah! Did you see my uncle on the night of his uprising?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Did he pray in the Mosque of Suhayl?' He said, 'Where is the Mosque of Suhayl? Do you mean the Mosque of Sahlah?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Verily, if he had prayed two Rak’ah there and then sought refuge with Allāh, He would have protected him for one year.' Abū Ḥamzah said to him, 'May I sacrifice my father and mother for you! Are you referring to this (known) Mosque of Sahlah?' He said, 'Yes.'

It contains the house of Ibrāhīm where he used to rise against the giants. It contains the house of Idrīs where he used to sew. It contains the place where the rider ties his camel. It contains a green rock which has the pictures of the prophets within it, and the clay under this rock is the clay from which Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, created the prophets. The Mi’rāj (ascension) took place in it, and it is the great Fārūq (separator). A part of it is a place, and it is the route people will pass. It is part of Kūfān, and the trumpet will be blown in it, and to it is the gathering. Seventy thousand people will be resurrected from its side and they will enter Paradise without any judgment.

Those are the ones whom Allāh has set aright and upon whom He has increased His blessings. Verily they are the devout winners who will be rewarded before others. They love to repel any praise about themselves and they are terrified of meeting Allāh with His justice. They are quick in obeying Allāh, they perform good deeds, and they understand that Allāh sees what they do. There will not be any judgment nor torment for them. Verily Allāh removes the rancour and purifies the believers.
From its middle moved the mountain of Ahwāz, and a time has come upon it and it was populated.

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ خُرُوجِهِ: The night of his uprising (referring to Imam al-Ḥasan or Imam al-Ḥusayn)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and historical merits of the Mosque of Sahlah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) highlights the unique spiritual status of the Mosque of Sahlah in Kūfah, where a simple two-rak’ah prayer with seeking refuge grants a year of divine protection. This narration, found in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, situates the mosque as a profound eschatological site containing the 'Blue Stone' with prophet images, the clay of creation, and the Mi'raj, serving as a gathering place for seventy thousand who enter Paradise without reckoning. This reflects the Shia tradition of attributing deep metaphysical and historical layers to specific geographic sanctuaries in Iraq.
